content: Copper aspirinate, also known as Copper(II) aspirinate, is a chemical compound formed by the chelation of aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) with copper(II) cations (Cu²⁺). This compound has been utilized in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Copper aspirinate can be synthesized through various methods. One common preparation involves dissolving an excess amount of acetylsalicylic acid in an aqueous solution of sodium carbonate. It is important to note that sodium hydroxide is unsuitable for this process, as it hydrolyzes acetylsalicylic acid into salicylic acid and sodium acetate, which would interfere with the desired reaction. After dissolving the acetylsalicylic acid, the solution is filtered to remove any undissolved material. The filtered solution is then mixed with a solution containing Cu²⁺ cations, such as copper(II) sulfate. This reaction immediately precipitates bright blue crystals of copper aspirinate. These crystals are subsequently filtered, washed, and recrystallized to purify the product. The use of an excess of acetylsalicylic acid in the initial step is critical, as it prevents unreacted carbonate anions from precipitating copper during the reaction. Medicinally, copper aspirinate has been demonstrated to be an effective therapeutic agent for managing rheumatoid arthritis. In addition to its medicinal applications, copper aspirinate has also been explored for its potential use as a pigment in materials such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polystyrene.
